title: Reconnect a bathroom-sink pop-up stopper to its pivot rod
instruction: Reconnect the drain stopper to its pivot rod.
context: Done by: general maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5 million) and plumbers. A pop-up stopper that has come off its pivot rod is a common lavatory repair. The stand holds the drain body as it sits under a basin, with the pivot port facing the worker. The eye the rod must pass through is inside the drain, out of sight. A rod pushed in under or beside it seats its ball and looks done, but the stopper no longer opens and closes.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Drain body (fixed): a chrome brass bathroom-sink pop-up drain body, a round tube 40 mm across with a 32 mm bore, standing upright in a bench stand (dark grey steel base plate 100 x 100 x 8 mm and a grey clamp collar 56 mm square, 22 mm tall round the tube's foot), its axis 33 cm in front of the arm bases and 5 cm left of the midline. On top, a chrome flange 60 mm across and 4 mm thick, its top 110 mm up. The pivot port points straight at the robot, its axis 54 mm up: a spout with a 16 mm round bore ending 40 mm from the drain's axis, a white plastic seat washer with a 9 mm round hole 20 to 23 mm from the axis, and an opening through the tube wall 12 mm tall and about 12 mm wide at the bore (15 mm at the outside). Pop-up stopper (loose, 55 g, about 112 mm long): a chrome head 38 mm across and 9 mm thick with a 12 mm knob on top, resting closed on the flange; under it, a dark plastic cross of guide fins 30.5 mm across and 50 mm long, a 9 mm stem and, at the bottom, an eye: a ring 17 mm across and 5 mm thick with a 9 mm round hole, its centre 82 mm below the head, so 28 mm up, 26 mm below the port. The eye's hole runs left to right, across the port. Pivot rod (loose, 40 g): a steel rod 5 mm across and 250 mm long with a white plastic pivot ball 14 mm across and 10 mm long, the ball's centre 42 mm from the rod's inner end. It lies front to back, inner end toward the drain, the ball's centre 24.2 cm in front and 5 cm right of the midline, the rod's axis 30 mm up, in the 6 mm notches of two dark grey steel rest blocks, each 12 mm front to back, 20 mm wide and 27.5 mm tall, with a cheek 7 mm wide and 3 mm tall either side of the notch, so the cheeks reach 30.5 mm, centred 30 mm in front of and 180 mm behind the ball's centre. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Everything is checked from outside the drain, once the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the rod or the stopper) and both parts have been still for 1 s. Readings: the rod comes out of the spout's 16 mm bore, and its outer end is at most 199 mm from the spout's end face, measured along the rod with a rule (196 mm with the ball home on the seat washer); the stopper's head is centred within 4 mm on the flange, upright within 6 degrees, and its underside between 1 mm below and 40 mm above the flange top (depth gauge from the basin). Movement test, right after, to show the rod is through the stopper's eye (the pivot nut and lift linkage are left out, so the pushes go on the rod's outer end, where the linkage's strap would clamp, and on the stopper's knob): 1. with a push-pull gauge, push the rod's outer end up, rising steadily to 0.2 N over 0.5 s and held 0.5 s: the stopper's head must drop at least 3 mm on the depth gauge; 2. ease the push off steadily over 1 s and wait 1 s: the stopper must have risen again at least 3 mm; 3. with a spring scale hooked on the knob, pull straight up with a steady 1 N (about twice the stopper's weight) for 0.5 s: it may rise at most 10 mm, because the rod catches it. A rod beside, over or short of the eye moves nothing in steps 1 and 2; a stopper resting on a rod under its eye lifts off in step 3; both fail. Score 1.0 when the readings and the test pass. Score 0.5 when the test passes but the outer end is more than 199 mm from the spout (ball not home). Score 0 otherwise, including either part still held. If a gripper comes within 5 mm of either part during or after the test, the check starts again from the 1 s of stillness.
reset_notes: 1. Take the rod out of the port and lay it front to back in the notches of the two rest blocks, inner end toward the drain, the ball's centre 24.2 cm in front and 5 cm right of the midline (the rest blocks are 12 mm long front to back, 20 mm wide, 27.5 mm tall, centred 30 mm in front of and 180 mm behind the ball's centre). 2. Turn the stopper so its eye's hole runs left to right, a quarter turn from facing the port. 3. Then lower it until its head rests on the flange. 4. Run with -E object_jitter=0. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Real sizes, masses and round bores; holes are rings of overlapping cylinders. The pivot ball is a round barrel. The pivot nut, gasket, clevis strap and lift rod are left out: they go on after the rod is in the eye and don't decide engagement, and the simulator's thread can't start from separate parts. With no nut, only its seat keeps the ball in the port, and the rod's outer end drops and holds the stopper partly open. The movement test's pushes are steady forces applied by the scorer.
scores: Dream-1 run (revised scorer, 1,200 steps): 0.0, arms moved but never reached the parts, so the test never ran; demo: 1.0 (movement test passed: drop 11.2 mm, back 12.0 mm, pull rise 6.5 mm; outer end 197.8 mm from the spout)
